title: Reserve pool scaleback and price tuning playbook
summary: Playbook to manage reserve burst pools, trigger scaleback of contractor/on-call headcount, and pin pricing levers across hosted/dedicated/private offerings under demand shocks.
body:
Context:
- Goal: create an operationalized finance playbook that (1) preserves SLA-backed throughput for enterprise customers, (2) avoids permanent headcount expansion after transient token spikes, and (3) provides clear price/tier signals to product and sales.

High-level approach:
1) Maintain a small committed reserve pool (GPUs equivalent) with a 3-tier activation policy: 'Warm' (10% extra), 'Hot' (30% extra), 'Emergency' (50% extra).
2) Tie automatic scaleback rules to a combination of rolling 72h average token usage + spot GPU price index + revenue retention signal (churn risk > 4%).
3) Use pricing nudges instead of blunt rate increases where possible: temporary surcharge credits, ephemeral priority lanes, or per-customer soft throttles.

Headcount & contracting triggers (operational):
- Baseline (steady): 0 extra contractors; maintain 2 on-call infra engineers (SRE pool).
- Warm activation (>10% sustained over 8h): bring 2 contractors for burst ops; 1 additional sales engineer for churn watches.
- Hot activation (>30% sustained over 4h OR spot GPU price > 1.8x baseline for 6h): bring 6 contractors and 2 temporary SREs; pause noncritical hiring.
- Emergency (>50% or multi-region failure): tactical hiring freeze + escalate to Exec for price tier decision.

Quick sensitivity model (summary lines) — a small extract of the sheet: 
- Inputs: baseline-token-rate=1.0B/day, baseline-gpu-cost-per-hour=$3.5, committed-pool=120 GPU-hrs/day, avg-ondemand-premium=1.7x
- Scenario A (mild spike + price stable): +20% tokens -> incremental cost = +$8.4k/week -> prefer contractor + dynamic batching -> Headcount delta = +4 contractors (4 wks), expected net margin hit = -1.2 p.p.
- Scenario B (sustained surge + spot price up 60%): +40% tokens -> incremental cost = +$27k/week -> recommend temporary slab price increase for top 5% customers OR convert a portion to dedicated reservations; Headcount delta = +10 contractors (8 wks), net margin hit = -3.6 p.p. unless priced.
- Scenario C (extreme multi-region shock): +120% tokens, spot price x2.2 -> incremental cost = +$150k/week -> immediate Exec-level pricing action: temporary priority surcharge + customer credits for migration; Headcount delta = +20 contractors + cross-team on-call rotation, margin hit > -10 p.p.

Operational pricing levers (ordered by preference):
- 1) Soft priority lanes: sell ephemeral priority for customers (1-7 days) as an opt-in.
- 2) Per-route micro-surcharge on particularly heavy routes (embedding-heavy pipelines).
- 3) Reserved capacity upsell with short-term discounts (3 month commits) to shift load predictably.
- 4) Direct per-token surcharge as last resort; prefer explicit product features first.

Cost-offset playbook (how finance pairs with product):
- Fast quantization push: finance to sponsor a 2-week engineering sprint to move high-volume customers to a quantized variant (estimated 12-18% cost saving). Trigger when scenario incremental cost exceeds $20k/week.
- Smart-batching rollout: prioritize customers with lots of short-notes requests; expected 8-12% saving for selected cohort; finance to fund customer migration credits.
- Early-bird conversion offers: for customers in Hot tier, offer 10% discount to convert 3 months of usage to a Dedicated seat.

Headcount phasing table (textual):
- Week 0 (trigger): +contractors (pool ops) hired via vendor A (standard 4 wk onboarding).
- Week 1-4: monitor weekly retention + net new revenue from upsells; if <40% of incremental cost recovered, extend contractor hires week-by-week (cap at 12 weeks).
- Week 6: review replace-with-perm decision for up to 30% of contractor pool if consecutive months >30% delta.

Contingency budget buckets (proposed):
- Tier 1 reserve (operational immediate): $200k cash buffer for 6 weeks of contractor + spot cost cover.
- Tier 2 strategic: $500k runway buffer that can be deployed to accelerate quantization or buy regional reserved capacity.

Decision thresholds (operational checklist):
- If 72h rolling increase >25% AND expected persistence >7 days -> elevate to Finance Ops + Product + Sales for pricing pathing.
- If spot GPU price >1.8x baseline for >24h -> automatically enable batching and quantization suggestions in Optimize portal; notify customers in top 10% of usage.
- If churn risk >6% for any top 20 customers -> immediate sales outreach + temporary credits + pricing negotiation.

Example runbook excerpt (for finance ops):
- Step 1: Pull 72h rolling token delta and spot index (FIN dashboard).
- Step 2: Run the sensitivity tab (sheet) — produces expected incremental cost and headcount need.
- Step 3: If activation criteria met, request contractors from vendor with 48h SLA; open Jira FIN-EMERG-xxx.
- Step 4: Draft pricing communications (product + legal) for temporary priority lanes and send to top 50 customers within 6h.

Open questions / risks:
- Vendor capacity: can preferred contractor vendors scale to +20% within 72h? (Liam to confirm).
- Signal reliability: rolling 72h metric is noisy for highly bursty traffic (embedding spikes). Consider median-of-windows filter.
- Sales & CS alignment: how to avoid pushing customers to competitors if we enforce surcharges.

Action items (short):
- [ ] Finalize 3-tier numeric thresholds and codify in the FIN dashboard (Owner: Aisha, ETA: 2026-11-10).
- [ ] Vendor capacity confirmation and contingency vendor list (Owner: Ravi, ETA: 2026-11-05).
- [ ] Draft customer messaging templates for Warm/Hot/Emergency price signals (Owner: Mei, ETA: 2026-11-08).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intended as a lightweight operational sheet (not the full proforma). Please comment with missing assumptions (esp. GPU $/hr baseline and typical per-route token mixes).
- I intentionally left the full per-customer sensitivity matrix truncated — will attach the detailed CSV after vendor capacity confirmation.
